title: AhnLab: Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers on the official SoftwareOK site were tampered with to install a Python RAT
date_note: The ASEC post gives only its publication day; it states no date for the tampering.
place: SoftwareOK (location not stated in the source)
geo_basis: no place stated in the source
summary: AhnLab's ASEC says some Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed on the official SoftwareOK website had been tampered with to contain malicious files. Confirmed so far are Q-Dir 12.85.0.0, 12.84.0.0 and 12.83.0.0 and DesktopOK 12.85.0.0 and 12.82.0.0. The files install a Python-based remote access trojan, and ASEC says the cause and path of the replacement have not been identified.
plain: AhnLab says some Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers from the official SoftwareOK site were altered to install a remote access trojan. It says how the files were replaced is not yet known.
exec: AhnLab says software downloaded from a vendor's official site carried a remote access trojan; the way the files were replaced is unidentified.
action: AhnLab advises checking SHA-256 hashes against the official page, reinstalling the latest version, and checking for suspicious Python environments, scheduled tasks and external traffic; reinstalling alone may not remove the RAT.

evidence.quote: some Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed on the official SoftwareOK website had been tampered with to contain malicious files

validation.note: Only the AhnLab ASEC analysis was read; SoftwareOK's own statement was not found.
